title: Santapogue Neck
summary: Santapogue is recorded as a neck of land in Babylon, south of the settlement of Breslau, now Lindenhurst.
history_content: Santapogue was one of the five meadow necks bought in 1659. The name appears in Huntington records by 1669 with spellings including Santtapauge, Santapauge, Santepaug, and Santepogue.
translation_content:
Santapogue is interpreted as "a place of cool water," probably named for a cold spring on the neck.

Why Place Names Matter

“The act of renaming geographical names in the Indigenous language is part of a decolonizing project and is a way to make visible the connection to the land, to the knowledge connected to it, and to a cultural heritage.”

— Coppélie Cocq, Traditional knowledge – New experts (2017), Article discussion of Indigenous-language geographical naming
preservation_content: Santapogue links the south-shore meadow necks of Babylon with Native water-place naming and seventeenth-century land records.
